original_card.question: Can the native P104 low-rank channel be completed with a legal, fully charged I-G/2 side correction?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier.

first_step.inspect: Read the P104 open next questions and its fixed local histogram; inspect why appending I-G/2 after source completion is not justified. #1991 supplies the checked native channel, not the missing correction.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one exact side-correction cut and bound its allowed cost from a favorable completed moment at a declared target. Stop or hand off if the necessary source/target access cannot be justified or even the optimistic total misses the target.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.

actual_scope: Exact minimum dimension-gap cost for 0..104 integral flows in PR #2163's optimistic P104 single-cut nested-contact graph at cut 2429; source-bound primal/dual certificate and conditional budget arithmetic.
scope_change_reason: Take Discussion #2164's released first handoff. Price a necessary communication relaxation before attempting a side-correction word; this does not meet the original constructive admission gate.
bottleneck_link: The binding complex P104 route has a free nested-contact capacity result but an unpriced exchange. The sharp price shows what this fixed-cut relaxation would require a changed coverage contract to credit; it does not close arbitrary changed-path mechanisms.
stop_rule: Stop after a primal/dual optimum or a concrete failure of the network model. Do not build a correction when the one-way relaxation already exceeds the inherited no-progress-credit slack. Reserve final work for controls and handoff.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json: cost C(F)=9 max(0,F-8), F=0..104; cost 864 at 104, eight free paths and 96 price 9 paths. Independent acceptance checks conservation/capacity, dual gap 9 and penalty 72, and a Gaussian-elimination replay of 1427 layers/399680 unit edges. Seven test groups contain 15 rejecting controls. Conditional zero-saving moment 8523/7592 under unchanged idle obligations; no new kappa.

open_questions.question: Can a changed coverage contract credit the productive progress of one actual changed P104 path enough to pass its complete moment?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The fixed-cut one-way graph price864 exceeds the unchanged-obligation slack 328/9; frame nesting alone is not a cheap escape.
open_questions.first_step: Specify one changed trajectory and its exact owner/idle obligation changes, then evaluate a favorable fully charged moment before synthesizing the word.
open_questions.blocked_by: No such ownership/coverage identity or dirty-restored schedule is supplied; flow paths are not scalar circuits.

open_questions.question: Does a simultaneous paid-contact model at several explicitly chosen cuts have a materially lower exact price?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The present theorem fixes cut 2429 and does not constrain changed timing of added contacts.
open_questions.first_step: State the changed cut set and contact-capacity semantics, check current overlap, then apply the same primal/dual screen and stop if its favorable price already fails the intended budget.
open_questions.blocked_by: A useful changed contract and priced restoration must be specified; another free max-flow result would not establish admission.

selection.choice: Suggested p104-side-correction, refined to the released minimum-cost handoff; helper-inventory and rank-shape suggestions passed over for this concrete bounded question.
